issues_confirmed: .github/workflows/build-exe.yml:41 — the release zip packages only supplier_scraper.exe, config.ini, README.md and SETUP_GUIDE.pdf. cities_us.txt is not included, and `git log -p --follow .github/workflows/build-exe.yml` shows it was never included in any revision since the distribution system landed in f38f5bd.

standalone/cli.py:22-28 and standalone/web_server.py:566,627 — when frozen, all three read cities_us.txt from Path(sys.executable).parent (beside the exe). standalone/supplier_scraper.spec:16-17 bundles it into PyInstaller `datas`, which unpacks to sys._MEIPASS; web_server.py:32 is the repo's only _MEIPASS use and it covers templates/ only. The bundled copy is therefore unreachable and the beside-the-exe copy does not exist, so --all-us and --resume are unavailable in every shipped build (cli.py:261 exits; web_server.py:667 redirects with 'No cities loaded').

standalone/web_server.py:577-580 — with no cities file, num_cities=0 so total_areas_possible=0; standalone/templates/scrape.html:46 then renders '0 / 0 city×term combinations searched', :47 hides the progress bar, and :71 offers 'iterate all 0 city × term combinations'. Visible symptom on the client's dashboard.

standalone/web_server.py:151-161 vs :537 — _sent_today() builds today_start from date.today() (LOCAL midnight, naive) but EmailLog.created_at is written with datetime.utcnow() (naive UTC). Verified by simulation in TZ=Asia/Karachi (UTC+5): an email sent at local 00:00 stores 19:00 on the previous UTC date and is NOT counted; the first counted hour is local 05:00. Between local 00:00 and 05:00 _sent_today() returns 0, so the pre-flight check at :486 passes and the in-loop re-check at :516 never trips — the daily send cap is fully disabled for those five hours and resets mid-campaign at local midnight.

standalone/cli.py:311-384 — the CLI send command has no daily-cap check at all, while web_server.py:484-488 and :516 enforce one. Root README.md:34 instructs the client to use the uncapped CLI path. The two paths also disagree on throttle defaults: cli.py:325 falls back to 30/min, web_server.py:491 to 20/min.

standalone/places_scraper.py:38-40,61-65 — only raise_for_status() is called; the Google Places JSON 'status' field (REQUEST_DENIED / OVER_QUERY_LIMIT / INVALID_REQUEST, all returned with HTTP 200) is never read. grep for 'status' in places_scraper.py still matches only raise_for_status.

standalone/places_scraper.py:195 — mark_done() is called unconditionally after the per-place loop, so an area that returned zero results because of an API error is recorded as scraped; standalone/area_manager.py:13-22 then skips it for rescrape_days (default 30), poisoning --resume.
standalone/places_scraper.py:47-54 — pagination sleeps a fixed 2s before reusing next_page_token and does not detect INVALID_REQUEST, so a not-yet-warm token silently truncates results from 60 to 20.

standalone/email_sender.py:114-115 — every exception (timeout, transient 4xx) returns success:False; callers at standalone/web_server.py:523 and standalone/cli.py:359 write email_status='bounced', which is permanent because the send query requires email_status=='pending' (web_server.py:458, cli.py:332) and /contacts/{id}/reset (web_server.py:214-225) only clears 'approved'. 'bounced' is additionally overloaded as the unsubscribe sentinel at web_server.py:235, so the dashboard tile at :172 conflates three states.

standalone/web_server.py:248,280-292 — /contacts/duplicates loads all non-unsubscribed traders into memory and runs a full pairwise SequenceMatcher comparison, O(n^2), against a stated target of 10,000+ traders.

README.md:74,81,83 — the release runbook still names the Gist manifest version.json, but standalone/update_checker.py:15 was changed to Supplier_Scraper.json in commit a08e1a3 precisely because the old name 404'd silently; update_checker.py:47-48 swallows all errors.

standalone/requirements_standalone.txt:6-7 — pins beautifulsoup4==4.12.3 and lxml>=5.2.1, but `grep -rn 'bs4|BeautifulSoup|lxml' standalone/` returns nothing; email extraction is pure regex (website_email_extractor.py:8). Dead deps installed on every tagged CI build, and lxml is unpinned in the pipeline that produces the client artifact.

standalone/cities_us.txt — 13 duplicate city lines out of 267 (Akron OH, Arvada CO, Billings MT, Costa Mesa CA, Eugene OR, Glendale CA, Henderson NV, Inglewood CA, Lansing MI, Palmdale CA, Peoria IL, Rancho Cucamonga CA, Tallahassee FL); each wastes a Text Search call per term against the 10k/month cap in billing_guard.py:24-25.
standalone/billing_guard.py:64 — the counter is incremented before the HTTP request is made, so failed requests still consume free-tier budget.

standalone/places_scraper.py:192 and :102 — _save_trader is called with no try/except and commits inline; an IntegrityError on the google_place_id unique constraint (models.py:32) — the CLI+web concurrency billing_guard's own docstring anticipates — propagates out of run_places_scrape, which has only `finally: db.close()`, killing the entire run.

standalone/website_email_extractor.py:29,44 — up to 6 sequential fetches at 8s timeout each (~48s worst case per place), and the worst case is the no-email path whose result is discarded. It returns raw HTML as website_text, which keyword_classifier.score_company:59-63 substring-matches, so a product keyword in a CSS class or nav menu earns the full +30.
standalone/web_server.py:66-70 — the _setup_guard middleware re-reads and re-parses config.ini from disk on every HTTP request.
standalone/validator.py:40 — returns True when no Hunter.io/ZeroBounce key is configured, so email_valid means 'unchecked', not 'verified'.

standalone/tests/test_core.py:107-119 — build_email_body is tested with a company name and with an unknown placeholder but never with company_name=None, which is exactly the compose-preview path (web_server.py:427) that commit a08e1a3 had to fix by hand. This is the single missing assertion closest to the most recent bug-shaped commit.

standalone/models.py:29,45,52 use naive datetime.utcnow() while standalone/job_registry.py:12-13 uses aware datetime.now(UTC); utcnow() also emits a DeprecationWarning on the Python 3.14 the repo targets.

Branch agent/2026-09-20-google-places-error-statuses-are-never-c is zero commits ahead of main (empty diff) — the previous review's top item was never implemented. No source file has changed since a08e1a3.

Only 4 of the 12 unit tests run (test_job_registry.py); test_core.py errors on `import sqlalchemy`. proposed_tasks: [BUG] Add cities_us.txt to the release zip (build-exe.yml:41) and give the three read sites a _MEIPASS fallback — --all-us and --resume are dead in every shipped build

[BUG] Fix the daily send cap: _sent_today() compares local midnight to UTC timestamps so the cap is off 00:00-05:00 PKT, and cli.py send has no cap at all — share one implementation from email_sender.py
[BUG] Check the Google Places JSON status field in places_scraper.py and stop calling mark_done() when the search failed; add a regression test for REQUEST_DENIED
[BUG] Stop a transient SMTP failure from permanently marking a contact bounced — reset email_status or distinguish hard from soft failures
[QUICK WIN ~15min] Fix the Gist manifest filename in the root README release runbook (version.json -> Supplier_Scraper.json) before it silently breaks the update channel again
verdict: Good code, broken box: the modules are small, readable and genuinely tested, but the artifact the client actually downloads has never contained cities_us.txt, so the full-US scrape this product exists for has never worked outside the dev machine — and the daily send cap, the one guard protecting the client's Gmail account, is silently disabled for five hours every night. Nothing from the 2026-09-20 list was touched; the shipping pipeline now needs more attention than the code.
